newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes higher on crusher, export demand.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes higher on crusher, export demand.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher, boosted by crusher related buying, renewed export demand and a firm tone to CBOT soybeans, floor sources said.
They cited talk that Japan bought 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes of Canadian canola at an overnight tender. Gains were limited by hedge-related selling.
July canola closed $1.50 higher at $428.70 with new crop November up $1.70 at $389.70.
Flaxseed was mostly higher with some shorts taking profits after Tuesday's slide to contract lows.
Western barley futures were mostly steady as commercial buying offset local and hedge related selling. July barley closed unchanged at $138.10.
Feed wheat ended lower on hedge related and local selling. July was off $1.00 lower at $163.00.
Oats closed higher, realigning following recent strength in CBOT oats in two-sided commission house trade. October closed up US$1.00 at US$118.50. Feed peas remained tradeless.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
